C. Require annual AUP sign-off.
D. Use geofencing tools to unlock devices while on the premises.
cards.back: B. Implement containerization of company data.
cards.why: Containerization separates company data in an encrypted, managed workspace on a personal device, so it can be protected and wiped independently.

whyNot.A: A PIN protects device access but does not separate or protect company data specifically.
whyNot.C: An AUP sign-off is an administrative control with no technical enforcement of data storage.
whyNot.D: Geofencing restricts location-based access but does not securely store company data.

cards.front:
A web server, which is configured to use TLS with AES-GCM-256, SHA-384, and ECDSA, recently suffered an information loss breach. Which of the following is MOST likely the cause?
A. Insufficient key bit length
B. Weak cipher suite
C. Unauthenticated encryption method
D. Poor implementation
cards.why: The listed algorithms (TLS with AES-GCM-256, SHA-384, ECDSA) are strong, so a breach most likely stems from poor implementation or configuration.

whyNot.A: A 256-bit AES key and ECDSA are adequate lengths.
whyNot.B: AES-GCM with SHA-384 and ECDSA is a strong modern cipher suite.
whyNot.C: AES-GCM is an authenticated encryption mode, so this option is incorrect.

cards.front:
An incident involving a workstation that is potentially infected with a virus has occurred. The workstation may have sent confidential data to an unknown internet server. Which of the following should a security analyst do FIRST?
A. Make a copy of everything in memory on the workstation.
B. Turn off the workstation.
C. Consult information security policy.
D. Run a virus scan.
cards.back: A. Make a copy of everything in memory on the workstation.
cards.why: Memory is the most volatile evidence under the order of volatility, so capturing it first preserves running malware and connection data before it is lost.

whyNot.B: Powering off destroys volatile memory evidence such as active processes and connections.
whyNot.C: Policy should guide response, but evidence in memory can be lost while consulting it.
whyNot.D: A scan alters system state and may destroy evidence or alert the malware.

cards.front:
A vice president at a manufacturing organization is concerned about desktops being connected to the network. Employees need to log onto the desktops' local account to verify that a product is being created within specifications; otherwise, the desktops should be as isolated as possible. Which of the following is the BEST way to accomplish this?
A. Put the desktops in the DMZ.
B. Create a separate VLAN for the desktops.
C. Air gap the desktops.
D. Join the desktops to an ad-hoc network.
cards.why: An air gap physically isolates the desktops from all networks, while still allowing local logins to verify product specifications.

whyNot.A: A DMZ exposes systems to the internet-facing boundary and is not isolation.
whyNot.B: A VLAN is only logical separation and the desktops remain connected to the network.
whyNot.D: An ad-hoc network still provides network connectivity and is not isolation.

cards.front:
An in-house penetration tester has been asked to evade a new DLP system. The tester plans to exfiltrate data through steganography. Discovery of which of the following would help catch the tester in the act?
A. Abnormally high numbers of outgoing instant messages that contain obfuscated text
B. Large-capacity USB drives on the tester's desk with encrypted zip files
C. Outgoing emails containing unusually large image files
D. Unusual SFTP connections to a consumer IP address
cards.back: C. Outgoing emails containing unusually large image files
cards.why: Steganography typically hides data inside carrier files such as images, so unusually large outgoing image files in email would suggest hidden data.

whyNot.A: Obfuscated text in instant messages suggests encoding, not steganography.
whyNot.B: Encrypted zip files on USB drives indicate encryption and physical exfiltration, not steganography.
whyNot.D: SFTP connections are encrypted transfers, not data hidden within another file.

cards.front:
A member of the admins group reports being unable to modify the "changes" file on a server. The permissions on the file are as follows: Permissions User Group File -rwxrw-r--+ Admins Admins changes Based on the output above, which of the following BEST explains why the user is unable to modify the "changes" file?
A. The SELinux mode on the server is set to "enforcing."
B. The SELinux mode on the server is set to "permissive."
C. An FACL has been added to the permissions for the file.
D. The admins group does not have adequate permissions to access the file.
cards.back: C. An FACL has been added to the permissions for the file.
cards.why: The trailing plus sign in the permissions indicates an extended ACL (FACL) is applied, which can override the basic group permissions and deny this user.

whyNot.A: SELinux enforcing mode is not indicated by the file permissions shown.
whyNot.B: Permissive mode only logs violations and would not block access.
whyNot.D: The group already has read and write permissions, so basic permissions are adequate.

cards.front:
A penetration tester is conducting an assessment on Comptia.org and runs the following command from a coffee shop while connected to the public Internet: c:\nslookup -querytype=MX comptia.org Server: Unknown Address: 198.51.100.45 comptia.org MX preference=10, mail exchanger = 92.68.102.33 comptia.org MX preference=20, mail exchanger = exchg1.comptia.org exchg1.comptia.org internet address = 192.168.102.67 Which of the following should the penetration tester conclude about the command output?
A. The public/private views on the Comptia.org DNS servers are misconfigured.
B. Comptia.org is running an older mail server, which may be vulnerable to exploits.
C. The DNS SPF records have not been updated for Comptia.org.
D. 192.168.102.67 is a backup mail server that may be more vulnerable to attack.
cards.back: D. 192.168.102.67 is a backup mail server that may be more vulnerable to attack.
cards.why: The secondary MX record points to a host with a private address, 192.168.102.67, which is a backup mail server that is often less hardened than the primary.

whyNot.A: Split DNS views may be questionable, but the output does not show a misconfiguration.
whyNot.B: The output reveals no mail server version or age.
whyNot.C: The output contains MX records only, with no SPF information.

cards.front:
A security analyst is inspecting the results of a recent internal vulnerability scan that was performed against intranet services. The scan reports include the following critical-rated vulnerability: Title: Remote Command Execution vulnerability in web server Rating: Critical (CVSS 10.0) Threat actor: any remote user of the web server Confidence: certain Recommendation: apply vendor patches Which of the following actions should the security analyst perform FIRST?
A. Escalate the issue to senior management.
B. Apply organizational context to the risk rating.
C. Organize for urgent out-of-cycle patching.
D. Exploit the server to check whether it is a false positive.
cards.back: B. Apply organizational context to the risk rating.
cards.why: Before acting, the analyst should apply organizational context, such as asset criticality and exposure, to validate the risk rating.

whyNot.A: Escalation without understanding business context is premature.
whyNot.C: Urgent patching may follow, but only after the context is assessed.
whyNot.D: Exploiting a production server is risky, and the scan confidence is already certain.

cards.front:
Company A agrees to provide perimeter protection, power, and environmental support with measurable goals for Company B, but will not be responsible for user authentication or patching of operating systems within the perimeter. Which of the following is being described?
A. Service level agreement
B. Memorandum of understanding
C. Business partner agreement
D. Interoperability agreement
cards.why: A service level agreement defines the services a provider delivers, measurable targets and responsibilities, which matches the scenario.

whyNot.B: An MOU expresses intent and typically lacks measurable service commitments.
whyNot.C: A business partner agreement governs the partnership terms, not specific service levels.
whyNot.D: An interoperability agreement covers technical compatibility between systems.

cards.front:
A company is deploying smartphones for its mobile salesforce. These devices are for personal and business use but are owned by the company. Sales personnel will save new customer data via a custom application developed for the company. This application will integrate with the contact information stored in the smartphones and will populate new customer records onto it. The customer application's data is encrypted at rest, and the application's connection to the back office system is considered secure. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) has concerns that customer contact information may be accidentally leaked due to the limited security capabilities of the devices and the planned controls. Which of the following will be the MOST efficient security control to implement to lower this risk?
A. Implement a mobile data loss agent on the devices to prevent any user manipulation with the contact information.
B. Restrict screen capture features on the devices when using the custom application and the contact information.
C. Restrict contact information storage dataflow so it is only shared with the customer application.
D. Require complex passwords for authentication when accessing the contact information.
cards.back: C. Restrict contact information storage dataflow so it is only shared with the customer application.
cards.why: Restricting contact information so it flows only to the custom application is data flow control, which limits accidental leakage at the source.

whyNot.A: A mobile DLP agent that blocks all user manipulation is heavy-handed and impractical on limited devices.
whyNot.B: Blocking screen capture addresses only one leak path.
whyNot.D: Complex passwords protect access but do not prevent leakage of contact data to other applications.

cards.front:
The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) is asking for ways to protect against zero-day exploits. The CISO is concerned that an unrecognized threat could compromise corporate data and result in regulatory fines as well as poor corporate publicity. The network is mostly flat, with split staff/guest wireless functionality. Which of the following equipment MUST be deployed to guard against unknown threats?
A. Cloud-based antivirus solution, running as local admin, with push technology for definition updates
B. Implementation of an off-site datacenter hosting all company data, as well as deployment of VDI for all client computing needs
C. Host-based heuristic IPS, segregated on a management VLAN, with direct control of the perimeter firewall ACLs
D. Behavior-based IPS with a communication link to a cloud-based vulnerability and threat feed
cards.back: D. Behavior-based IPS with a communication link to a cloud-based vulnerability and threat feed
cards.why: A behavior-based IPS detects anomalous activity rather than relying on known signatures, and a cloud threat feed adds fresh intelligence, which together address unknown zero-day threats.

whyNot.A: Antivirus relies on definitions and running as local admin increases risk; it cannot recognize truly unknown exploits.
whyNot.B: Moving data off-site with VDI changes where data lives but does not detect or block unknown threats.
whyNot.C: Host-based heuristic IPS on a management VLAN with firewall control does not cover the flat network or guest wireless traffic.

cards.front:
An organization has several production-critical SCADA supervisory systems that cannot follow the normal 30- day patching policy. Which of the following BEST maximizes the protection of these systems from malicious software?
A. Configure a firewall with deep packet inspection that restricts traffic to the systems.
B. Configure a separate zone for the systems and restrict access to known ports.
C. Configure the systems to ensure only necessary applications are able to run.
D. Configure the host firewall to ensure only the necessary applications have listening ports
cards.back: C. Configure the systems to ensure only necessary applications are able to run.
cards.why: Application whitelisting lets only approved executables run, so malware cannot execute on unpatched SCADA systems regardless of which vulnerabilities exist.

whyNot.A: Deep packet inspection filters network traffic but does not stop malicious software introduced by other paths such as removable media.
whyNot.B: Network zoning and port restriction limit exposure but do not prevent malware from running on the host.
whyNot.D: A host firewall controlling listening ports does not stop unauthorized applications from executing.

cards.front:
An organization identifies a number of hosts making outbound connections to a known malicious IP over port TCP 80. The organization wants to identify the data being transmitted and prevent future connections to this IP. Which of the following should the organization do to achieve this outcome?
A. Use a protocol analyzer to reconstruct the data and implement a web-proxy.
B. Deploy a web-proxy and then blacklist the IP on the firewall.
C. Deploy a web-proxy and implement IPS at the network edge.
D. Use a protocol analyzer to reconstruct the data and blacklist the IP on the firewall.
cards.back: D. Use a protocol analyzer to reconstruct the data and blacklist the IP on the firewall.
cards.why: A protocol analyzer can reconstruct the captured traffic to reveal what data was sent, and blacklisting the known malicious IP on the firewall blocks future connections.

whyNot.A: A web proxy does not reveal data already transmitted and is unnecessary when a firewall blacklist blocks the IP.
whyNot.B: A proxy and blacklist block traffic but nothing here identifies the data that was already transmitted.
whyNot.C: A proxy and edge IPS do not reconstruct past transmissions and are heavier than needed to block one known IP.

cards.front:
Legal authorities notify a company that its network has been compromised for the second time in two years. The investigation shows the attackers were able to use the same vulnerability on different systems in both attacks. Which of the following would have allowed the security team to use historical information to protect against the second attack?
A. Key risk indicators
B. Lessons learned
C. Recovery point objectives
D. Tabletop exercise
cards.why: A lessons learned review after the first incident documents the exploited vulnerability and remediation, giving historical information to prevent the same attack recurring.

whyNot.A: Key risk indicators monitor risk levels but do not capture specifics of a past incident's root cause.
whyNot.C: Recovery point objectives define acceptable data loss, not how to prevent repeat exploitation.
whyNot.D: A tabletop exercise rehearses response scenarios and does not itself record past incident findings.

cards.front:
A small company's Chief Executive Officer (CEO) has asked its Chief Security Officer (CSO) to improve the company's security posture quickly with regard to targeted attacks. Which of the following should the CSO conduct FIRST?
A. Survey threat feeds from services inside the same industry.
B. Purchase multiple threat feeds to ensure diversity and implement blocks for malicious traffic
C. Conduct an internal audit against industry best practices to perform a qualitative analysis.
D. Deploy a UTM solution that receives frequent updates from a trusted industry vendor.
cards.back: A. Survey threat feeds from services inside the same industry.
cards.why: Surveying threat feeds from the same industry is a quick, low-cost way to learn which targeted attacks apply to the company before investing in controls.

whyNot.B: Buying many feeds and blocking traffic spends money before determining which intelligence is relevant to the company.
whyNot.C: An internal audit with qualitative analysis is slow and does not quickly address targeted attacks.
whyNot.D: Deploying a UTM is a purchase and implementation step that should follow understanding the specific threats.

cards.front:
During a routine vulnerability assessment, the following command was successful: echo "vrfy 'perl -e 'print "hi" x 500 ' ' " | nc www.company.com 25 Which of the following vulnerabilities is being exploited?
A. Buffer overflow directed at a specific host MTA
B. SQL injection directed at a web server
C. Cross-site scripting directed at www.company.com
D. Race condition in a UNIX shell script
cards.back: A. Buffer overflow directed at a specific host MTA
cards.why: The command sends a VRFY request with 500 repeated characters to SMTP port 25, an attempt to overflow a buffer in the mail transfer agent.

whyNot.B: No SQL syntax is present and the target is the SMTP service on port 25, not a web database.
whyNot.C: Cross-site scripting needs script injected into web content; this input goes to a mail server.
whyNot.D: A race condition exploits timing between operations, while this input is simply an oversized string.

cards.front:
A forensic investigator has run into difficulty recovering usable files from a SAN drive. Which of the following SAN features might have caused the problem?
A. Storage multipaths
B. Deduplication
C. iSCSI initiator encryption
D. Data snapshots
cards.why: Deduplication stores a single copy of repeated blocks and replaces others with pointers, so recovering complete, contiguous files from raw drives is difficult for forensics.

whyNot.A: Multipathing provides redundant paths to storage and does not alter how file data is stored.
whyNot.C: Initiator encryption protects data in transit over iSCSI and does not affect recovering data stored on the drive.
whyNot.D: Snapshots preserve point-in-time copies and typically help rather than hinder recovery.

cards.front:
A company offers SaaS, maintaining all customers' credentials and authenticating locally. Many large customers have requested the company offer some form of federation with their existing authentication infrastructures. Which of the following would allow customers to manage authentication and authorizations from within their existing organizations?
A. Implement SAML so the company's services may accept assertions from the customers' authentication servers.
B. Provide customers with a constrained interface to manage only their users' accounts in the company's active directory server.
C. Provide a system for customers to replicate their users' passwords from their authentication service to the company's.
D. Use SOAP calls to support authentication between the company's product and the customers' authentication servers.
cards.back: A. Implement SAML so the company's services may accept assertions from the customers' authentication servers.
cards.why: SAML provides federated single sign-on in which the company accepts signed assertions from customers' identity providers, letting customers manage authentication and authorization themselves.

whyNot.B: Customers would still be managing accounts inside the company's directory rather than their own infrastructure.
whyNot.C: Replicating passwords to the company duplicates credentials and defeats customer-controlled authentication.
whyNot.D: SOAP is a messaging protocol, not a federation standard that conveys authentication and authorization assertions.

cards.front:
A software development manager is taking over an existing software development project. The team currently suffers from poor communication due to a long delay between requirements documentation and feature delivery. This gap is resulting in an above average number of security- related bugs making it into production. Which of the following development methodologies is the team MOST likely using now?
A. Agile
B. Waterfall
C. Scrum
D. Spiral
cards.why: Waterfall is a sequential model with long gaps between requirements and delivery, so late testing and stale requirements let security bugs reach production.

whyNot.A: Agile uses short iterations with frequent delivery and communication, which contradicts a long delay.
whyNot.C: Scrum is an Agile framework built on short sprints and close communication.
whyNot.D: Spiral uses iterative cycles with risk analysis at each phase, so gaps would be shorter.

cards.front:
Following the successful response to a data-leakage incident, the incident team lead facilitates an exercise that focuses on continuous improvement of the organization's incident response capabilities. Which of the following activities has the incident team lead executed?
A. Lessons learned review
B. Root cause analysis
C. Incident audit
D. Corrective action exercise
cards.why: A lessons learned review after incident response identifies what worked and what to improve, driving continuous improvement of incident response capabilities.

whyNot.B: Root cause analysis finds why the incident occurred rather than improving overall response capability.
whyNot.C: An incident audit checks compliance with procedures and is not an improvement-focused exercise.
whyNot.D: Corrective action exercise is not a standard incident response phase for post-incident improvement.

cards.front:
A security analyst is attempting to break into a client's secure network. The analyst was not given prior information about the client, except for a block of public IP addresses that are currently in use. After network enumeration, the analyst's NEXT step is to perform:
A. a risk analysis.
B. a vulnerability assessment.
C. a gray-box penetration test.
D. an external security audit.
E. a red team exercise.
cards.why: With only IP ranges provided, the analyst has limited knowledge, and after enumeration the next step of actively probing for weaknesses fits a gray-box penetration test.

whyNot.A: A risk analysis evaluates likelihood and impact and is not the next technical step after enumeration.
whyNot.B: A vulnerability assessment identifies weaknesses without exploiting them, unlike the stated goal of breaking in.
whyNot.D: An external security audit reviews compliance and controls rather than attempting to break in.
whyNot.E: A red team exercise is a broad adversary simulation, not a step following enumeration.

cards.keyDoubt: B: Scanning for vulnerabilities is the normal step after enumeration, and with no prior information the test is black-box, not gray-box.

cards.front:
A security architect has convened a meeting to discuss an organization's key management policy. The organization has a reliable internal key management system, and some argue that it would be best to manage the cryptographic keys internally as opposed to using a solution from a third party. The company should use:
A. the current internal key management system.
B. a third-party key management system that will reduce operating costs.
C. risk benefits analysis results to make a determination.
D. a software solution including secure key escrow capabilities.
cards.back: C. risk benefits analysis results to make a determination.
cards.why: Choosing between internal and third-party key management is a business decision best made by weighing risks and benefits of each option.

whyNot.A: Keeping the current system by default ignores evaluating whether outsourcing has advantages.
whyNot.B: Choosing a third party solely for lower cost ignores security and risk considerations.
whyNot.D: Key escrow is a feature, not a way to decide between internal and external management.

cards.front:
After a recent internal breach, a company decided to regenerate and reissue all certificates used in the transmission of confidential information. The company places the greatest importance on confidentiality and non-repudiation, and decided to generate dual key pairs for each client. Which of the following BEST describes how the company will use these certificates?
A. One key pair will be used for encryption and decryption. The other will be used to digitally sign the data.
B. One key pair will be used for encryption. The other key pair will provide extended validation.
C. Data will be encrypted once by each key, doubling the confidentiality and non-repudiation strength.
D. One key pair will be used for internal communication, and the other will be used for external communication.
cards.back: A. One key pair will be used for encryption and decryption. The other will be used to digitally sign the data.
cards.why: Dual key pairs separate duties: one pair encrypts and decrypts for confidentiality, while the other signs data for non-repudiation.

whyNot.B: Extended validation concerns certificate identity vetting and is not a function of a second key pair.
whyNot.C: Double encryption does not provide non-repudiation, which requires digital signatures.
whyNot.D: Splitting keys by internal and external use does not address confidentiality and non-repudiation.

cards.front:
A security manager is creating an account management policy for a global organization with sales personnel who must access corporate network resources while traveling all over the world. Which of the following practices is the security manager MOST likely to enforce with the policy? (Select TWO)
A. Time-of-day restrictions
B. Password complexity
C. Location-based authentication
D. Group-based access control
E. Standard naming convention
cards.back:
B. Password complexity
D. Group-based access control
cards.why: Password complexity protects accounts used over untrusted networks, and group-based access control simplifies granting sales staff consistent resource access globally.

whyNot.A: Time-of-day restrictions would block travelers working across many time zones.
whyNot.C: Location-based authentication would conflict with personnel who access resources from anywhere in the world.
whyNot.E: A naming convention aids administration but does not secure access for traveling users.

cards.front:
A security administrator learns that PII, which was gathered by the organization, has been found in an open forum. As a result, several C-level executives found their identities were compromised, and they were victims of a recent whaling attack. Which of the following would prevent these problems in the future? (Select TWO).
A. Implement a reverse proxy.
B. Implement an email DLP.
C. Implement a spam filter.
D. Implement a host-based firewall.
E. Implement a HIDS.
cards.back:
B. Implement an email DLP.
C. Implement a spam filter.
cards.why: Email DLP prevents sensitive PII from leaving via email, and a spam filter reduces phishing and whaling messages reaching executives.

whyNot.A: A reverse proxy protects servers from inbound web requests and does not stop PII leakage or whaling emails.
whyNot.D: A host-based firewall filters network connections and does not inspect email content for phishing or PII.
whyNot.E: A HIDS detects host intrusions and does not prevent data leakage or whaling emails.

cards.front:
A security engineer is configuring a wireless network with EAP-TLS. Which of the following activities is a requirement for this configuration?
A. Setting up a TACACS+ server
B. Configuring federation between authentication servers
C. Enabling TOTP
D. Deploying certificates to endpoint devices
cards.back: D. Deploying certificates to endpoint devices
cards.why: EAP-TLS uses mutual certificate authentication, so both the RADIUS server and every client endpoint need X.509 certificates deployed before they can connect.

whyNot.A: TACACS+ is for device administration AAA and is not required for EAP-TLS, which typically uses RADIUS.
whyNot.B: Federation links identity providers across domains and is not part of EAP-TLS configuration.
whyNot.C: TOTP is a one-time password method, and EAP-TLS authenticates with certificates rather than OTP codes.

cards.front:
Ann is the IS manager for several new systems in which the classification of the systems' data are being decided. She is trying to determine the sensitivity level of the data being processed. Which of the following people should she consult to determine the data classification?
A. Steward
B. Custodian
C. User
D. Owner
cards.why: The data owner is the senior role accountable for the data and is responsible for deciding its classification and sensitivity level.

whyNot.A: A steward handles day-to-day data quality and governance, but the owner makes the classification decision.
whyNot.B: A custodian implements and maintains controls for the data, but does not decide its classification.
whyNot.C: A user simply consumes the data and has no authority to classify it.

cards.front:
A systems administrator wants to generate a self-signed certificate for an internal website. Which of the following steps should the systems administrator complete prior to installing the certificate on the server?
A. Provide the private key to a public CA.
B. Provide the public key to the internal CA.
C. Provide the public key to a public CA.
D. Provide the private key to the internal CA.
E. Provide the public/private key pair to the internal CA
F. Provide the public/private key pair to a public CA.
cards.back: D. Provide the private key to the internal CA.
cards.why: A self-signed certificate for an internal site is normally issued through an internal CA, which signs the certificate request built from the server's public key. Key escrow of the private key is not part of that process.

whyNot.A: Private keys must never be given to a public CA, and a public CA does not sign internal self-signed certificates.
whyNot.B: Providing only the public key to an internal CA is the correct practice, but the key marks this option as incorrect.
whyNot.C: A public CA is not needed for internal sites and would not issue a self-signed certificate.
whyNot.E: Sharing the full key pair, including the private key, with any CA exposes the private key.
whyNot.F: Sending a key pair to a public CA exposes the private key and is unnecessary for an internal site.

cards.keyDoubt: B. Only the public key (in a CSR) goes to the internal CA, while the private key must stay secret on the server, so D is wrong.

cards.front:
Which of the following controls allows a security guard to perform a post-incident review?
A. Detective
B. Preventive
C. Corrective
D. Deterrent
cards.why: The key marks this as corrective, but a post-incident review of what happened is a detective activity, since it examines evidence after the event to identify what occurred.

whyNot.A: Detective controls identify and review events after they occur, which matches a guard reviewing an incident afterward.
whyNot.B: Preventive controls stop incidents before they happen, and a post-incident review does not.
whyNot.D: Deterrent controls discourage attackers, such as signs or visible guards, rather than review events.

cards.keyDoubt: A. A guard reviewing an incident after it occurs is a detective activity, not corrective remediation.

cards.front:
Attackers have been using revoked certificates for MITM attacks to steal credentials from employees of Company.com. Which of the following options should Company.com implement to mitigate these attacks?
A. Captive portal
B. OCSP stapling
C. Object identifiers
D. Key escrow
E. Extended validation certificate
cards.why: OCSP stapling has the server deliver a signed, timestamped certificate status response during the TLS handshake, so clients can reliably detect revoked certificates.

whyNot.A: A captive portal redirects users for network authentication and does not check certificate revocation.
whyNot.C: Object identifiers label certificate fields and policies and do not verify revocation status.
whyNot.D: Key escrow stores copies of private keys for recovery and does not stop use of revoked certificates.
whyNot.E: An extended validation certificate strengthens identity vetting but does not address revocation checking.

cards.front:
After attempting to harden a web server, a security analyst needs to determine if an application remains vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. Which of the following would BEST assist the analyst in making this determination?
A. tracert
B. Fuzzer
C. nslookup
D. Nmap
E. netcat
cards.why: A fuzzer sends malformed and unexpected input to an application, which helps reveal injection flaws such as SQL injection after hardening.

whyNot.A: tracert maps the network path to a host and says nothing about application vulnerabilities.
whyNot.C: nslookup queries DNS records and cannot test input handling.
whyNot.D: Nmap discovers hosts and open ports and does not test application input for SQL injection.
whyNot.E: netcat opens raw connections and can send data, but it does not systematically test for injection flaws.

cards.front:
A company is allowing a BYOD policy for its staff. Which of the following is a best practice that can decrease the risk of users jailbreaking mobile devices?
A. Install a corporately monitored mobile antivirus on the devices.
B. Prevent the installation of applications from a third-party application store.
C. Build a custom ROM that can prevent jailbreaking.
D. Require applications to be digitally signed.
cards.back: D. Require applications to be digitally signed.
cards.why: Jailbreaking often relies on installing unsigned code, so requiring digitally signed applications blocks that unverified code from running on the device.

whyNot.A: Mobile antivirus detects malware but does not stop users from jailbreaking their devices.
whyNot.B: Blocking third-party stores reduces risky apps but does not by itself prevent the jailbreak process.
whyNot.C: A custom ROM is impractical across BYOD devices and is itself a modification of the stock operating system.

cards.keyDoubt: B. Blocking third-party app stores is the more common best-practice control, though D is also defensible.

cards.front:
Which of the following describes the key difference between vishing and phishing attacks?
A. Phishing is used by attackers to steal a person's identity.
B. Vishing attacks require some knowledge of the target of attack.
C. Vishing attacks are accomplished using telephony services.
D. Phishing is a category of social engineering attack.
cards.back: C. Vishing attacks are accomplished using telephony services.
cards.why: Vishing is voice phishing, carried out over telephony services such as phone calls or VoIP, which distinguishes it from email-based phishing.

whyNot.A: Both vishing and phishing can be used to steal identities, so this does not distinguish them.
whyNot.B: Both attacks may use target research, so this is not the key difference.
whyNot.D: Phishing being a social engineering category is true but does not describe how vishing differs.

cards.front:
Which of the following should a security analyst perform FIRST to determine the vulnerabilities of a legacy system?
A. Passive scan
B. Aggressive scan
C. Credentialed scan
D. Intrusive scan
cards.why: A passive scan observes traffic without sending probes, so it is the safest first step for a fragile legacy system that could crash under active testing.

whyNot.B: Aggressive scans send heavy probing that could destabilize a fragile legacy system.
whyNot.C: A credentialed scan needs account access and is more invasive, so it is not the safest first step.
whyNot.D: Intrusive scans actively exploit or stress the system and risk disrupting a legacy host.

cards.front:
Which of the following components of printers and MFDs are MOST likely to be used as vectors of compromise if they are improperly configured?
A. Embedded web server
B. Spooler
C. Network interface
D. LCD control panel
cards.why: An embedded web server provides remote management, and if left with default credentials or unpatched it exposes the device to network-based compromise.

whyNot.B: The spooler queues print jobs and is less commonly the remote attack vector.
whyNot.C: The network interface is the transport path, while the exposed management service is the real weakness.
whyNot.D: The LCD panel requires physical access and is not a remote vector.

cards.front:
A hacker has a packet capture that contains: Which of the following tools will the hacker use against this type of capture?
A. Password cracker
B. Vulnerability scanner
C. DLP scanner
D. Fuzzer
cards.why: A capture holding hashed or captured credentials is attacked offline with a password cracker, which recovers plaintext passwords from the captured data.

whyNot.B: A vulnerability scanner probes live systems for weaknesses and does not analyze captured credentials.
whyNot.C: A DLP scanner detects sensitive data leaving an organization and is a defensive tool.
whyNot.D: A fuzzer sends malformed input to applications and does not process packet captures.

cards.front:
A user downloads and installs an MP3 converter, and runs the application. Upon running the application, the antivirus detects a new port in a listening state. Which of the following has the user MOST likely executed?
A. RAT
B. Worm
C. Ransomware
D. Bot
cards.why: A remote access Trojan hides in seemingly useful software and opens a listening port so the attacker can control the system remotely.

whyNot.B: A worm self-propagates across networks rather than being installed from a downloaded utility with a listening port.
whyNot.C: Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment, and does not typically show a new listening port.
whyNot.D: A bot connects out to a command server and is less characterized by a local listening port.

cards.front:
An attacker exploited a vulnerability on a mail server using the code below. Which of the following BEST explains what the attacker is doing?
A. The attacker is replacing a cookie.
B. The attacker is stealing a document.
C. The attacker is replacing a document.
D. The attacker is deleting a cookie.
cards.back: C. The attacker is replacing a document.
cards.why: The code shown cannot be verified here, so the key's answer that the attacker is replacing a document cannot be confirmed from the question text provided.

whyNot.A: Without the code, nothing indicates cookie manipulation.
whyNot.B: Without the code, nothing indicates the attacker is reading or exfiltrating a document.
whyNot.D: Without the code, nothing indicates cookie deletion.

cards.front:
A security analyst is securing smartphones and laptops for a highly mobile workforce. Priorities include: Remote wipe capabilities Geolocation services Patch management and reporting Mandatory screen locks Ability to require passcodes and pins Ability to require encryption Which of the following would BEST meet these requirements?
A. Implementing MDM software
B. Deploying relevant group policies to the devices
C. Installing full device encryption
D. Removing administrative rights to the devices
cards.why: Mobile device management centrally enforces remote wipe, geolocation, patch reporting, screen locks, passcodes, and encryption across smartphones and laptops.

whyNot.B: Group policies cover domain-joined Windows machines and do not manage smartphones or remote wipe.
whyNot.C: Full device encryption covers only encryption and none of the other listed requirements.
whyNot.D: Removing admin rights limits user changes but provides no remote wipe, geolocation, or reporting.

cards.front:
A technician receives a device with the following anomalies: Frequent pop-up ads Show response-time switching between active programs Unresponsive peripherals The technician reviews the following log file entries: File Name Source MD5 Target MD5 Status antivirus.exe F794F21CD33E4F57890DDEA5CF267ED2 F794F21CD33E4F57890DDEA5CF267ED2 Automatic iexplore.exe 7FAAF21CD33E4F57890DDEA5CF29CCEA AA87F21CD33E4F57890DDEAEE2197333 Automatic service.exe 77FF390CD33E4F57890DDEA5CF28881F 77FF390CD33E4F57890DDEA5CF28881F Manual USB.exe E289F21CD33E4F57890DDEA5CF28EDC0 E289F21CD33E4F57890DDEA5CF28EDC0 Stopped Based on the above output, which of the following should be reviewed?
A. The web application firewall
B. The file integrity check
C. The data execution prevention
D. The removable media control
cards.why: The iexplore.exe row shows different source and target MD5 hashes, meaning the file was altered, which is exactly what a file integrity check reveals.

whyNot.A: A web application firewall protects web servers and is unrelated to local file hash mismatches.
whyNot.C: Data execution prevention blocks code running from memory regions and is not indicated by these hash logs.
whyNot.D: Removable media control relates to USB.exe, whose hashes match, so it is not the anomaly.

cards.front:
A CSIRT has completed restoration procedures related to a breach of sensitive data is creating documentation used to improve the organization's security posture. The team has been specifically tasked to address logical controls in their suggestions. Which of the following would be MOST beneficial to include in lessons learned documentation? (Choose two.)
A. A list of policies, which should be revised to provide better clarity to employees regarding acceptable use
B. Recommendations relating to improved log correlation and alerting tools
C. Data from the organization's IDS/IPS tools, which show the timeline of the breach and the activities executed by the attacker
D. A list of potential improvements to the organization's NAC capabilities, which would improve AAA within the environment
E. A summary of the activities performed during each phase of the incident response activity
F. A list of topics that should be added to the organization's security awareness training program based on weaknesses exploited during the attack
cards.back:
A. A list of policies, which should be revised to provide better clarity to employees regarding acceptable use
F. A list of topics that should be added to the organization's security awareness training program based on weaknesses exploited during the attack
cards.why: Lessons learned should drive logical-control improvements; better log correlation and alerting (SIEM) and NAC/AAA enhancements are technical, logical controls that address detection and access gaps revealed by the breach.

whyNot.A: Policy revisions are administrative controls, not logical controls, which the team was specifically tasked to address.
whyNot.C: IDS/IPS timeline data is incident evidence, not a recommendation for improving controls in lessons learned.
whyNot.E: A phase-by-phase activity summary documents what happened but does not propose logical control improvements.
whyNot.F: Awareness training topics are administrative controls, not logical controls.

cards.keyDoubt: B and D: the task specifies logical controls, so log correlation/alerting tools and NAC/AAA improvements fit, while policy and training are administrative.

cards.front:
An organization plans to implement multifactor authentication techniques within the enterprise network architecture. Each authentication factor is expected to be a unique control. Which of the following BEST describes the proper employment of multifactor authentication?
A. Proximity card, fingerprint scanner, PIN
B. Fingerprint scanner, voice recognition, proximity card
C. Smart card, user PKI certificate, privileged user certificate
D. Voice recognition, smart card, proximity card
cards.back: A. Proximity card, fingerprint scanner, PIN
cards.why: True multifactor authentication combines different factor categories: something you have (proximity card), something you are (fingerprint), and something you know (PIN).

whyNot.B: Fingerprint and voice recognition are both inherence factors, and only the card is a different factor.
whyNot.C: Smart card, user certificate, and privileged certificate are all something-you-have factors.
whyNot.D: Voice is inherence while smart card and proximity card are both possession, so only two factor types appear.

cards.front:
Upon entering an incorrect password, the logon screen displays a message informing the user that the password does not match the username provided and is not the required length of 12 characters. Which of the following secure coding techniques should a security analyst address with the application developers to follow security best practices?
A. Input validation
B. Error handling
C. Obfuscation
D. Data exposure
cards.why: Error handling should return generic messages; revealing that the password does not match the username and details of length requirements leaks information useful to attackers.

whyNot.A: Input validation checks the data submitted, not the content of messages returned to the user.
whyNot.C: Obfuscation hides code logic and does not govern login error messages.
whyNot.D: Data exposure is a broader category; the specific coding flaw here is verbose, improper error handling.

cards.front:
Which of the following is the BEST reason to run an untested application is a sandbox?
A. To allow the application to take full advantage of the host system's resources and storage
B. To utilize the host systems antivirus and firewall applications instead of running it own protection
C. To prevent the application from acquiring escalated privileges and accessing its host system
D. To increase application processing speed so the host system can perform real-time logging
cards.back: C. To prevent the application from acquiring escalated privileges and accessing its host system
cards.why: A sandbox isolates an untested application so it cannot escalate privileges or reach the host system, containing any malicious or buggy behavior.

whyNot.A: Sandboxes deliberately restrict resource and storage access rather than granting full access.
whyNot.B: Sandboxes provide isolation and do not exist to substitute for application-level protections via host antivirus.
whyNot.D: Sandboxing typically adds overhead and does not increase processing speed.

cards.front:
A security technician has been receiving alerts from several servers that indicate load balancers have had a significant increase in traffic. The technician initiates a system scan. The scan results illustrate that the disk space on several servers has reached capacity. The scan also indicates that incoming internet traffic to the servers has increased. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of the decreased disk space?
A. Misconfigured devices
B. Logs and events anomalies
C. Authentication issues
D. Unauthorized software
cards.why: Rising inbound traffic combined with full disks suggests unauthorized software, such as malware or a staging tool, is consuming storage and generating or receiving traffic.

whyNot.A: Misconfigured devices would not typically explain both exhausted disk space and increased inbound internet traffic.
whyNot.B: Log anomalies are a symptom to investigate and do not by themselves explain the cause of disk exhaustion.
whyNot.C: Authentication issues cause login failures and lockouts, not disk consumption.

cards.keyDoubt: B: log growth from the traffic surge is a plausible cause of full disks, though D is the commonly accepted key.

cards.front:
A security administrator is diagnosing a server where the CPU utilization is at 100% for 24 hours. The main culprit of CPU utilization is the antivirus program. Which of the following issue could occur if left unresolved? (Select TWO)
A. MITM attack
B. DoS attack
C. DLL injection
D. Buffer overflow
E. Resource exhaustion
cards.back:
B. DoS attack
E. Resource exhaustion
cards.why: Sustained 100% CPU from the antivirus is resource exhaustion, which degrades availability and can effectively produce a denial of service for the server's legitimate functions.

whyNot.A: A man-in-the-middle attack involves intercepting traffic and is unrelated to local CPU load.
whyNot.C: DLL injection is an attack technique and not a consequence of high CPU utilization.
whyNot.D: Buffer overflow is a memory-handling flaw and does not result from sustained CPU load.

cards.front:
Which of the following is used to validate the integrity of data?
A. CBC
B. Blowfish
C. MD5
D. RSA
cards.why: MD5 is a hashing algorithm, and hashes are used to verify data integrity by detecting changes.

whyNot.A: CBC is a block cipher mode of operation providing confidentiality, not an integrity check.
whyNot.B: Blowfish is a symmetric encryption cipher used for confidentiality.
whyNot.D: RSA is an asymmetric algorithm used for encryption and signatures, not simple integrity hashing.

cards.front:
A user typically works remotely over the holidays using a web-based VPN to access corporate resources. The user reports getting untrusted host errors and being unable to connect. Which of the following is MOST likely the case?
A. The certificate has expired
B. The browser does not support SSL
C. The user's account is locked out
D. The VPN software has reached the seat license maximum
cards.why: An untrusted host error on a web-based VPN after a long absence most likely means the server's TLS certificate has expired and is no longer trusted.

whyNot.B: Modern browsers support SSL/TLS, and the user previously connected successfully.
whyNot.C: A locked account produces authentication errors, not untrusted host certificate warnings.
whyNot.D: Seat license limits would produce a capacity error, not a certificate trust error.

cards.front:
When it comes to cloud computing, if one of the requirements for a project is to have the most control over the systems in the cloud, which of the following is a service model that would be BEST suited for this goal?
A. Infrastructure
B. Platform
C. Software
D. Virtualization
cards.why: Infrastructure as a Service gives the customer the most control, including the OS, middleware, and applications, with only hardware and virtualization managed by the provider.

whyNot.B: PaaS leaves the OS and runtime managed by the provider, reducing customer control.
whyNot.C: SaaS offers the least control since the provider manages the entire application stack.
whyNot.D: Virtualization is a technology and not a cloud service model.

cards.front:
A security analyst is acquiring data from a potential network incident. Which of the following evidence is the analyst MOST likely to obtain to determine the incident?
A. Volatile memory capture
B. Traffic and logs
C. Screenshots
D. System image capture
cards.why: For a network incident, traffic captures and logs are the most relevant evidence because they show communications and events across the network.

whyNot.A: Volatile memory capture is host-focused and better suited to investigating a single system.
whyNot.C: Screenshots are limited, easily incomplete, and offer little forensic value for network analysis.
whyNot.D: A system image captures a single host's disk and is not primarily network evidence.

cards.front:
A cybersecurity analyst is looking into the payload of a random packet capture file that was selected for analysis. The analyst notices that an internal host had a socket established with another internal host over a non-standard port. Upon investigation, the origin host that initiated the socket shows this output: Given the above output, which of the following commands would have established the questionable socket?
A. traceroute 8.8.8.8
B. ping -1 30 8.8.8.8 -a 600
C. nc -1 192.168.5.1 -p 9856
D. pskill pid 9487
cards.why: Netcat (nc) creates arbitrary TCP sockets on specified ports, so an nc command using port 9856 would establish a connection over a non-standard port.

whyNot.A: Traceroute maps network hops using ICMP or UDP and does not establish a socket on a custom port.
whyNot.B: Ping sends ICMP echo requests and does not create a TCP socket on a port.
whyNot.D: pskill terminates a process and does not create any network connection.

cards.front:
A security administrator has written a script that will automatically upload binary and text-based configuration files onto a remote server using a scheduled task. The configuration files contain sensitive information. Which of the following should the administrator use? (Select TWO)
A. TOPT
B. SCP
C. FTP over a non-standard pot
D. SRTP
E. Certificate-based authentication
F. SNMPv3
cards.back:
C. FTP over a non-standard pot
E. Certificate-based authentication
cards.why: Sensitive files sent by an unattended script need encrypted transfer and non-interactive authentication; certificate-based authentication works for automation, and SCP encrypts the transfer.

whyNot.A: TOTP requires a changing code, which cannot be supplied by an unattended scheduled script.
whyNot.C: FTP on a non-standard port still sends data and credentials in cleartext.
whyNot.D: SRTP secures real-time voice and video media, not file transfers.
whyNot.F: SNMPv3 is for network device management and not file uploading.

cards.keyDoubt: B: SCP encrypts the file transfer, whereas FTP over a non-standard port remains unencrypted; B and E are the best pair.

cards.front:
A security analyst conducts a manual scan on a known hardened host that identifies many non- compliant items. Which of the following BEST describe why this has occurred? (Select TWO)
A. Privileged-user certificated were used to scan the host
B. Non-applicable plugins were selected in the scan policy
C. The incorrect audit file was used
D. The output of the report contains false positives
E. The target host has been compromised
cards.back:
B. Non-applicable plugins were selected in the scan policy
D. The output of the report contains false positives
cards.why: A hardened host showing many non-compliant items suggests scan misconfiguration, such as non-applicable plugins, along with false positives in the report.

whyNot.A: Privileged credentials typically improve scan accuracy and would not cause many non-compliant findings.
whyNot.C: An incorrect audit file is a plausible cause but is not the intended answer for this key.
whyNot.E: A compromised host would not be indicated simply by many compliance mismatches on a hardened system.

cards.front:
Which of the following solutions should an administrator use to reduce the risk from an unknown vulnerability in a third-party software application?
A. Sandboxing
B. Encryption
C. Code signing
D. Fuzzing
cards.why: Sandboxing isolates the application so that exploitation of an unknown vulnerability is contained and cannot easily affect the wider system.

whyNot.B: Encryption protects data confidentiality and does not mitigate exploitation of an application flaw.
whyNot.C: Code signing verifies origin and integrity but does not stop a signed application's unknown vulnerabilities.
whyNot.D: Fuzzing finds vulnerabilities during testing but is difficult with third-party code and does not reduce runtime risk.

cards.front:
A network administrator needs to allocate a new network for the R&D group. The network must not be accessible from the Internet regardless of the network firewall or other external misconfigurations. Which of the following settings should the network administrator implement to accomplish this?
A. Configure the OS default TTL to 1
B. Use NAT on the R&D network
C. Implement a router ACL
D. Enable protected ports on the switch
cards.back: A. Configure the OS default TTL to 1
cards.why: Setting the TTL to 1 ensures packets expire after a single hop and cannot be routed beyond the local network, regardless of firewall or external misconfiguration.

whyNot.B: NAT is not a security control and misconfiguration or port forwarding could still expose the network.
whyNot.C: A router ACL depends on correct configuration and can be misconfigured.
whyNot.D: Protected ports isolate hosts at layer 2 within a switch and do not prevent Internet reachability.

cards.front:
To help prevent one job role from having sufficient access to create, modify, and approve payroll data, which of the following practices should be employed?
A. Least privilege
B. Job rotation
C. Background checks
D. Separation of duties
cards.why: Separation of duties splits create, modify, and approve steps among different people, so no single role can complete a fraudulent payroll transaction alone.

whyNot.A: Least privilege limits each role to the access it needs, but one role could still legitimately need create, modify, and approve rights.
whyNot.B: Job rotation moves staff between roles periodically to expose fraud, but does not stop one role holding conflicting permissions.
whyNot.C: Background checks screen people before hiring and do not restrict what access a job role has.

cards.front:
When attackers use a compromised host as a platform for launching attacks deeper into a company's network, it is said that they are:
A. escalating privilege
B. becoming persistent
C. fingerprinting
D. pivoting
cards.why: Pivoting is using a compromised host as a stepping stone to attack other systems deeper inside the network that the attacker could not reach directly.

whyNot.A: Privilege escalation raises the attacker's rights on a system and does not describe using the host to reach other systems.
whyNot.B: Persistence means keeping access across reboots or credential changes, not launching attacks from the host.
whyNot.C: Fingerprinting identifies operating systems and services through probing and is reconnaissance, not attacking from a compromised host.

cards.front:
The help desk received a call after hours from an employee who was attempting to log into the payroll server remotely. When the help desk returned the call the next morning, the employee was able to log into the server remotely without incident. However, the incident occurred again the next evening. Which of the following BEST describes the cause of the issue?
A. The password expired on the account and needed to be reset
B. The employee does not have the rights needed to access the database remotely
C. Time-of-day restrictions prevented the account from logging in
D. The employee's account was locked out and needed to be unlocked
cards.back: C. Time-of-day restrictions prevented the account from logging in
cards.why: Failure only after hours, with success the next morning, indicates a time-of-day restriction on the account that limits when logins are permitted.

whyNot.A: An expired password would block logins at any hour and would stay broken until reset, not clear up by morning.
whyNot.B: Missing rights would cause failures at all times, not only in the evening.
whyNot.D: A lockout would persist until unlocked or the timer expires, and would not neatly recur each evening.

cards.front:
An analyst receives an alert from the SIEM showing an IP address that does not belong to the assigned network can be seen sending packets to the wrong gateway. Which of the following network devices is misconfigured and which of the following should be done to remediate the issue?
A. Firewall; implement an ACL on the interface
B. Router; place the correct subnet on the interface
C. Switch; modify the access port to trunk port
D. Proxy; add the correct transparent interface
cards.back: B. Router; place the correct subnet on the interface
cards.why: A host with an address outside the assigned subnet reaching the wrong gateway points to a router interface configured with the wrong subnet, fixed by assigning the correct one.

whyNot.A: An ACL filters traffic but does not correct which subnet an interface serves or the gateway addressing problem.
whyNot.C: Changing an access port to a trunk would carry multiple VLANs and would make the segmentation problem worse.
whyNot.D: A proxy mediates application traffic and does not define subnets or gateway addressing for the network.

cards.front:
A home invasion occurred recently in which an intruder compromised a home network and accessed a WiFI- enabled baby monitor while the baby's parents were sleeping. Which of the following BEST describes how the intruder accessed the monitor?
A. Outdated antivirus
B. WiFi signal strength
C. Social engineering
D. Default configuration
cards.why: Consumer IoT devices such as baby monitors often ship with default credentials and settings that attackers can easily find and use to gain access.

whyNot.A: Baby monitors do not typically run antivirus, and outdated antivirus is not how such devices are usually accessed.
whyNot.B: Signal strength affects range and reliability and does not grant an intruder access to the device.
whyNot.C: Nothing indicates the intruder tricked the occupants; the access came from weak device configuration.

cards.front:
A security engineer must install the same x.509 certificate on three different servers. The client application that connects to the server performs a check to ensure the certificate matches the host name. Which of the following should the security engineer use?
A. Wildcard certificate
B. Extended validation certificate
C. Certificate chaining
D. Certificate utilizing the SAN file
cards.back:
D. Certificate utilizing the SAN file

SAN = Subject Alternate Names
cards.why: A certificate with a Subject Alternative Name list can name several specific hostnames, so one certificate matches the host name check on all three servers.

whyNot.A: A wildcard covers subdomains of one domain, but the servers' names are not stated to share a domain, so the SAN is the safer fit.
whyNot.B: Extended validation certificates prove organizational identity more rigorously and do not address matching multiple host names.
whyNot.C: Certificate chaining links a certificate to its issuing CAs and does not make one certificate valid for several host names.

cards.front:
Which of the following refers to the term used to restore a system to its operational state?
A. MTBF
B. MTTR
C. RTO
D. RPO
cards.why: Mean time to repair (MTTR) is the average time needed to restore a failed system to its operational state.

whyNot.A: MTBF is the average time between failures and measures reliability, not how long restoration takes.
whyNot.C: RTO is the target maximum downtime allowed, a goal rather than the measured average repair time.
whyNot.D: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time, not the time to restore the system.

cards.front:
A Chief Information Officer (CIO) recently saw on the news that a significant security flaws exists with a specific version of a technology the company uses to support many critical application. The CIO wants to know if this reported vulnerability exists in the organization and, if so, to what extent the company could be harmed. Which of the following would BEST provide the needed information?
A. Penetration test
B. Vulnerability scan
C. Active reconnaissance
D. Patching assessment report
cards.why: A penetration test verifies whether the reported flaw exists and is exploitable, and shows the potential impact, which answers the CIO's question about extent of harm.

whyNot.B: A vulnerability scan can detect the flaw but does not demonstrate exploitation or the extent of possible damage.
whyNot.C: Active reconnaissance gathers information about targets and does not confirm exploitability or business impact.
whyNot.D: A patching assessment report shows patch status and does not measure how much harm the vulnerability could cause.

cards.front:
An organization is expanding its network team. Currently, it has local accounts on all network devices, but with growth, it wants to move to centrally managed authentication. Which of the following are the BEST solutions for the organization? (Select TWO)
A. TACACS+
B. CHAP
C. LDAP
D. RADIUS
E. MSCHAPv2
cards.why: TACACS+ and RADIUS are centralized AAA protocols that let network devices authenticate administrators against one central server instead of local accounts.

whyNot.B: CHAP is a challenge-response authentication method and does not provide centralized management of device accounts.
whyNot.C: LDAP is a directory access protocol, not the AAA protocol network devices typically use for administrator authentication.
whyNot.E: MSCHAPv2 is an authentication method carried inside other protocols and is not itself a centralized AAA solution.

cards.front:
An active/passive configuration has an impact on:
A. confidentiality
B. integrity
C. availability
D. non-repudiation
cards.why: Active/passive clustering keeps a standby system ready to take over if the active one fails, which improves availability.

whyNot.A: Confidentiality concerns preventing unauthorized disclosure, and a standby node does not change who can read data.
whyNot.B: Integrity concerns preventing unauthorized modification, which a failover configuration does not address.
whyNot.D: Non-repudiation proves who performed an action, which is unrelated to redundancy between nodes.

cards.front:
Which of the following would provide additional security by adding another factor to a smart card?
A. Token
B. Proximity badge
C. Physical key
D. PIN
cards.why: A smart card is something you have, so adding a PIN, which is something you know, creates two-factor authentication.

whyNot.A: A token is also something you have, so it adds a second item of the same factor type as the card.
whyNot.B: A proximity badge is another possession factor and does not add a different factor.
whyNot.C: A physical key is also something you have, so it duplicates the factor the smart card already provides.

cards.front:
A systems administrator wants to implement a wireless protocol that will allow the organization to authenticate mobile devices prior to providing the user with a captive portal login. Which of the following should the systems administrator configure?
A. L2TP with MAC filtering
B. EAP-TTLS
C. WPA2-CCMP with PSK
D. RADIUS federation
cards.back:
D. RADIUS federation

RADIUS generally includes 802.1X that pre-authenticates devices.
cards.why: RADIUS federation lets the network authenticate devices against a trusted RADIUS infrastructure before the user reaches the captive portal login.

whyNot.A: L2TP is a tunneling protocol and MAC filtering is weak, easily spoofed, and not a real authentication method.
whyNot.B: EAP-TTLS authenticates users or devices through a tunnel but needs a RADIUS back end, and federation is the fuller answer here.
whyNot.C: WPA2-CCMP with a PSK uses one shared key for everyone and cannot authenticate individual devices before the portal.

cards.front:
Which of the following uses precomputed hashes to guess passwords?
A. Iptables
B. NAT tables
C. Rainbow tables
D. ARP tables
cards.why: Rainbow tables are precomputed hash lookup tables that let an attacker quickly map hashes back to likely passwords.

whyNot.A: Iptables is a Linux firewall rule framework and has nothing to do with cracking password hashes.
whyNot.B: NAT tables map internal addresses to external ones and do not store password hashes.
whyNot.D: ARP tables map IP addresses to MAC addresses and do not contain hashes.

cards.front:
A Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) has tasked a security analyst with assessing the security posture of an organization and which internal factors would contribute to a security compromise. The analyst performs a walk-through of the organization and discovers there are multiple instances of unlabeled optical media on office desks. Employees in the vicinity either do not claim ownership or disavow any knowledge concerning who owns the media. Which of the following is the MOST immediate action to be taken?
A. Confiscate the media and dispose of it in a secure manner as per company policy.
B. Confiscate the media, insert it into a computer, find out what is on the disc, and then label it and return it to where it was found.
C. Confiscate the media and wait for the owner to claim it. If it is not claimed within one month, shred it.
D. Confiscate the media, insert it into a computer, make a copy of the disc, and then return the original to where it was found.
cards.back: A. Confiscate the media and dispose of it in a secure manner as per company policy.
cards.why: Unlabeled media of unknown origin may carry malware, so the most immediate safe action is to confiscate it and dispose of it securely per policy.

whyNot.B: Inserting unknown media into a computer risks executing malware, and returning it to the desks leaves the threat in place.
whyNot.C: Holding unclaimed unknown media for a month delays removing the risk and still leaves it available for use.
whyNot.D: Copying the disc requires inserting it into a computer, risking infection, and returning the original keeps the threat on the desks.

cards.front:
A company has noticed multiple instances of proprietary information on public websites. It has also observed an increase in the number of email messages sent to random employees containing malicious links and PDFs. Which of the following changes should the company make to reduce the risks associated with phishing attacks? (Select TWO)
A. Install an additional firewall
B. Implement a redundant email server
C. Block access to personal email on corporate systems
D. Update the X.509 certificates on the corporate email server
E. Update corporate policy to prohibit access to social media websites
F. Review access violation on the file server
cards.back:
C. Block access to personal email on corporate systems
E. Update corporate policy to prohibit access to social media websites
cards.why: Blocking personal email and restricting social media on corporate systems closes common phishing delivery channels and reduces where staff can be targeted and leak data.

whyNot.A: An additional firewall filters network traffic but does not stop users from opening malicious links and PDFs delivered by email.
whyNot.B: A redundant email server improves availability and does nothing to reduce phishing risk.
whyNot.D: Updating X.509 certificates on the mail server affects encryption and trust, not phishing messages sent to employees.
whyNot.F: Reviewing file server access violations addresses internal access control rather than the phishing delivery and leakage vectors described.

cards.front:
A security analyst is investigating a potential breach. Upon gathering, documenting, and securing the evidence, which of the following actions is the NEXT step to minimize the business impact?
A. Launch an investigation to identify the attacking host
B. Initiate the incident response plan
C. Review lessons learned captured in the process
D. Remove malware and restore the system to normal operation
cards.back: D. Remove malware and restore the system to normal operation
cards.why: After evidence is gathered and secured, eradication and recovery, removing malware and restoring normal operation, is the step that most directly limits ongoing business impact.

whyNot.A: Identifying the attacking host is investigative work and does not restore operations or reduce business impact.
whyNot.B: The incident response plan should already be running by the time evidence is being collected.
whyNot.C: Lessons learned is the final phase, after eradication and recovery.

cards.front:
Joe, a salesman, was assigned to a new project that requires him to travel to a client site. While waiting for a flight, Joe, decides to connect to the airport wireless network without connecting to a VPN, and the sends confidential emails to fellow colleagues. A few days later, the company experiences a data breach. Upon investigation, the company learns Joe's emails were intercepted. Which of the following MOST likely caused the data breach?
A. Policy violation
B. Social engineering
C. Insider threat
D. Zero-day attack
cards.why: Joe broke the company's acceptable use and remote access policy by using public Wi-Fi without a VPN to send confidential email, which exposed the data to interception.

whyNot.B: No one manipulated Joe into acting; he made the choice himself.
whyNot.C: Joe had no malicious intent, so this is not an insider threat; the interception came from an outside party.
whyNot.D: A zero-day is an unknown software flaw, and none was exploited here.

cards.front:
A company is performing an analysis of the corporate enterprise network with the intent of identifying what will cause losses in revenue, referrals, and/or reputation when out of commission. Which of the following is an element of a BIA that is being addressed?
A. Mission-essential function
B. Single point of failure
C. backup and restoration plans
D. Identification of critical systems
cards.back:
A. Mission-essential function

The BIA is composed of the following three steps: Determine mission/business processes and recovery criticality.
cards.why: A mission-essential function is a process whose loss would hurt revenue, referrals, or reputation, and a BIA identifies these to set recovery priorities.

whyNot.B: A single point of failure is a component whose failure stops a service, not a measure of revenue or reputation loss.
whyNot.C: Backup and restoration plans are recovery controls, not the BIA element that measures business loss.
whyNot.D: Identifying critical systems is related but focuses on technology assets rather than the business functions and their losses.

cards.front:
A company wants to ensure confidential data from storage media is sanitized in such a way that the drive cannot be reused. Which of the following method should the technician use?
A. Shredding
B. Wiping
C. Low-level formatting
D. Repartitioning
E. Overwriting
cards.why: Physical destruction by shredding makes the media unusable and unrecoverable, which is the only option here that guarantees the drive cannot be reused.

whyNot.B: Wiping sanitizes the data but leaves the drive reusable.
whyNot.C: Low-level formatting does not reliably remove data and leaves the drive usable.
whyNot.D: Repartitioning changes the partition table only and leaves the data recoverable.
whyNot.E: Overwriting destroys the data but the drive can still be reused.

cards.front:
A forensic expert is given a hard drive from a crime scene and is asked to perform an investigation. Which of the following is the FIRST step the forensic expert needs to take the chain of custody?
A. Make a forensic copy
B. Create a hash of the hard rive
C. Recover the hard drive data
D. Update the evidence log
cards.why: Chain of custody starts with documenting who received the evidence and when, so the evidence log is updated first, before anyone handles the drive.

whyNot.A: A forensic copy is made only after custody is documented and the original is protected.
whyNot.B: Hashing proves integrity but comes after custody is recorded.
whyNot.C: Recovering data modifies the working process and must come after documentation and imaging.

cards.front:
An incident response manager has started to gather all the facts related to a SIEM alert showing multiple systems may have been compromised. The manager has gathered these facts: The breach is currently indicated on six user PCs One service account is potentially compromised Executive management has been notified In which of the following phases of the IRP is the manager currently working?
A. Recovery
B. Eradication
C. Containment
D. Identification
cards.why: The manager is determining the scope and nature of the compromise from a SIEM alert, which is the identification phase.

whyNot.A: Recovery restores systems to normal operation, which has not begun.
whyNot.B: Eradication removes the threat, and no removal steps have been taken yet.
whyNot.C: Containment isolates affected systems, and the manager is still gathering facts.

cards.front:
A stock trading company had the budget for enhancing its secondary datacenter approved. Since the main site is a hurricane-affected area and the disaster recovery site is 100 mi (161 km) away, the company wants to ensure its business is always operational with the least amount of man hours needed. Which of the following types of disaster recovery sites should the company implement?
A. Hot site
B. Warm site
C. Cold site
D. Cloud-based site
cards.why: A cloud-based DR site can fail over automatically and be managed with minimal staff, which suits a company that must always be operational with the fewest man hours.

whyNot.A: A hot site meets uptime needs but requires significant staffing and cost to maintain and operate.
whyNot.B: A warm site needs hands-on setup and data sync before it can take over.
whyNot.C: A cold site needs the most time and labor to bring online.

cards.front:
User from two organizations, each with its own PKI, need to begin working together on a joint project. Which of the following would allow the users of the separate PKIs to work together without connection errors?
A. Trust model
B. Stapling
C. Intermediate CA
D. Key escrow
cards.why: A trust model, such as cross-certification or a bridge CA, lets each PKI trust certificates from the other, so users avoid certificate validation errors.

whyNot.B: OCSP stapling speeds up revocation checks but does not establish trust between separate PKIs.
whyNot.C: An intermediate CA extends a single hierarchy and does not link two independent PKIs.
whyNot.D: Key escrow stores keys for recovery and has no bearing on cross-PKI trust.

cards.front:
A security analyst is mitigating a pass-the-hash vulnerability on a Windows infrastructure. Given the requirement, which of the following should the security analyst do to MINIMIZE the risk?
A. Enable CHAP
B. Disable NTLM
C. Enable Kerebos
D. Disable PAP
cards.why: Pass-the-hash abuses NTLM hashes for authentication, so disabling NTLM removes the mechanism the attack depends on.

whyNot.A: CHAP is a challenge-response protocol for PPP links and does not address Windows NTLM hashes.
whyNot.C: Enabling Kerberos alone leaves NTLM available as a fallback, so the risk remains.
whyNot.D: PAP is a legacy cleartext protocol unrelated to Windows pass-the-hash.

cards.front:
A security analyst is reviewing an assessment report that includes software versions, running services, supported encryption algorithms, and permission settings. Which of the following produced the report?
A. Vulnerability scanner
B. Protocol analyzer
C. Network mapper
D. Web inspector
cards.why: A vulnerability scanner reports software versions, running services, supported ciphers, and permission settings to identify weaknesses.

whyNot.B: A protocol analyzer captures and decodes traffic and does not assess host configuration.
whyNot.C: A network mapper discovers hosts and open ports but does not audit permissions and cipher support in depth.
whyNot.D: A web inspector examines web page content and does not produce host-wide assessment reports.

cards.front:
A Chief Information Officer (CIO) asks the company's security specialist if the company should spend any funds on malware protection for a specific server. Based on a risk assessment, the ARO value of a malware infection for a server is 5 and the annual cost for the malware protection is $2500. Which of the following SLE values warrants a recommendation against purchasing the malware protection?
A. $500
B. $1000
C. $2000
D. $2500
cards.why: ALE equals SLE times ARO, so with an ARO of 5 the lowest SLE keeps annual loss at or below the $2500 control cost, making the purchase unjustified.

whyNot.B: An SLE of $1000 gives an ALE of $5000, which exceeds the $2500 cost and justifies buying protection.
whyNot.C: An SLE of $2000 gives an ALE of $10,000, so the control is clearly worth buying.
whyNot.D: An SLE of $2500 gives an ALE of $12,500, far above the cost of protection.

cards.front:
A recent internal audit is forcing a company to review each internal business unit's VMs because the cluster they are installed on is in danger of running out of computer resources. Which of the following vulnerabilities exist?
A. Buffer overflow
B. End-of-life systems
C. System sprawl
D. Weak configuration
cards.why: System sprawl is the uncontrolled growth of VMs that consumes cluster resources, which matches business units creating VMs until capacity runs out.

whyNot.A: A buffer overflow is a memory-handling code flaw and has nothing to do with resource exhaustion from VM count.
